name: self-improvement
conclusion: self-improvement (Act) specifies 4 of 5 categories: 1 autonomy limit, 3 clarification rules, 1 validation rule, 1 escalation rule; none for approval gates. Strongest: clarification rules.

autonomy_limits.conclusion: 1 autonomy limit (1 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly prose: applying a lesson without waiting for confirmation.

statements.quote: Don't wait for the user to confirm before applying the lesson within this conversation.

clarification_rules.conclusion: 3 clarification rules (2 mandatory, 1 advisory; 2 conditional), mostly prose: general frustration from the user; withdrawn or unverified assumptions; unsure factual corrections.

statements.quote: | General frustration | Could be any of the above — ask one clarifying question |
Offer the corrected version without it, or ask if the assumption is actually valid.
If unsure, say so rather than confabulating a fix.

validation.conclusion: 1 validation rule (1 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly list: verifying a fix before presenting it.

statements.quote: **Verify the fix before presenting it** — before closing the loop, ask internally: *"Does this actually solve the problem, or does it just look better?"* A fix that addresses the symptom but not the c

escalation.conclusion: 1 escalation rule (1 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly list: the same mistake recurring in the conversation.

statements.quote: **Flag if it's a pattern** — if this same type of mistake has appeared more than once in the conversation, say so: > "This is the second time I've [X] — I'll make a note of this."
